_contract: This is the shape of plan.replan_context, the block scripts/replan_trip.py writes into a
replanned plan. It is filled in below with a real example rather than nulls, because the
all-null stub this replaced told an author the field names and nothing about what belongs in
them -- and the one field that matters, must_reverify, is the one a stub cannot demonstrate.
replanned_from names the plan this was derived from, so a reader can find the artifact that
was superseded. replanned_at is the date the shift was run, not the date the trip starts.
changed_fields lists what the script rewrote mechanically. Every entry is a pure function of
the delta -- dates, day numbering, accommodation windows, dates prefilled into booking URLs.
Prose is never in this list, because the script never rewrites prose: a sentence like
'Saturday is the only full shopping day' becomes false when the dates move, and swapping the
weekday token inside it would turn a stale sentence into a confident one, which is worse.
must_reverify is the point of the whole block. One entry per fact the change invalidated,
each carrying the path that holds it and the reason it is now a guess.
check_plan_consistency.py FAILS the plan while any entry has resolved other than true, so a
replanned trip cannot be delivered until a human has re-checked each one at its original
source, written what they found into resolution, and set resolved: true.
Resolving means re-checking, not ticking. Where a reason begins CLOSED ON THE NEW DAY, do not
even re-check: the plan already carries its own refutation, so move the item to another day,
take the fallback the plan names, or drop it.
The example below is real. Shifting a Cologne trip from Fri 18 - Mon 21 September by one day
put day 2 on a Sunday (NRW law closes retail, and that day existed to buy allergy-safe food),
day 3 on a Monday (Museum Ludwig shuts Mondays), and day 4 on a Tuesday -- the one weekday the
Roemisch-Germanisches Museum is closed, and it had been chosen precisely because it opens on
Mondays when every other city museum does not. Three of four days lost their anchor to a
one-day shift, and the script found all of it by reading the plan's own sentences.
See references/replanning.md. Delete this _contract key before saving the real plan.
change_request: Push the whole trip back one day; the Friday morning meeting cannot move.
retained_note: Route order, stops, segment modes, fare bases, venue and accommodation choices and every budget row were kept: none of them depends on which weekday the trip starts. Ticket day_number and anchor planned_day were re-derived from the new dates rather than re-typed, because re-typing them by hand is the off-by-one that references/research-budget.md records.

must_reverify.reason: CLOSED ON THE NEW DAY. Day 3 now falls on Monday, and this card's own hours say the venue is shut Mondays. The plan refutes itself here -- do not re-check it, move the meal or take the named fallback.
Day 4 moved Monday -> Tuesday. This museum runs Wed-Mon and closes Tuesdays; it was chosen for being the one major museum open on a Monday, so the reason it is in the plan no longer holds.

Day 2 moved Saturday -> Sunday. This text promises the trip's only market and shopping day, and NRW law closes retail on Sunday. Prose is never rewritten by the script -- edit the sentence by hand once the day is re-planned.

Cleared by this replan. The verification report certified the old dates, and every weekday-keyed claim it checked is now unverified. Re-run the seven-agent pass in references/verification.md before calling this plan bookable.
